html:
Komitas was an Armenian priest, composer and collector of folk songs, born Soghomon Soghomonian in 1869 in Kütahya in western Anatolia, whose work made him the founder of modern Armenian music.

Orphaned young, he was sent to the seminary at Etchmiadzin and trained in music in Berlin. He collected thousands of Armenian and Kurdish folk songs from villages and showed how distinct Armenian music was. He arranged the Divine Liturgy for choir. In April 1915 he was among the Armenian intellectuals arrested in Constantinople at the start of the Armenian genocide. He was released but never recovered from what he saw, and spent his last years in psychiatric hospitals, dying near Paris in 1935. Much of what he collected was lost. Yerevan's music conservatory bears his name, as does a museum in Armenia.
sum: Komitas was an Armenian priest, composer and collector of folk songs, born Soghomon Soghomonian in 1869 in Kütahya in western Anatolia, whose work made him the founder of modern Armenian music.
